text:
mike: quick heads-up. after shrinking the RBAC for ns=priv-core the RBAC preflight probe returned OK but an hour later we observed outbound KMS calls to 203.0.113.45 from serviceAccount:key-manager-proxy. unsure if misconfig or host-level dns hijack. anyone oncall?

ops-bot: [ANOMALY] priv-core cluster egress to 203.0.113.45 detected 2026-09-02T11:12Z. 44 outbound TLS connections from system:serviceaccount:priv-core:key-manager-proxy.

anita: oncall. paste the exact kubectl patch and the preflight probe config. also capture the probe output (curl/traceroute) and the node /etc/hosts.

mike: patch I applied: `kubectl patch rolebinding priv-core-secrets -n priv-core --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/roleRef/name","value":"secrets-reader"}]'` at 11:02:18Z. preflight probe is a small curl to `https://kms.internal/healthz` run from the deployment init container. probe output showed HTTP/2 200 at 11:01:55.

sara: curious: the probe name resolves via CoreDNS to `kms.internal`. can you `kubectl exec` into a pod and run `getent hosts kms.internal` and `curl -v https://kms.internal/healthz --resolve` to see IP/SSL? also check node `/etc/hosts` and `iptables -t nat -L`.

mike: ran checks. `getent hosts kms.internal` -> `10.0.5.8` inside pod. but node `/etc/hosts` on node-12 had an entry `203.0.113.45 kms.internal` - likely a bootstrap/legacy migration artifact. pasted snippet:
```
# /etc/hosts excerpt
10.0.5.8 kms.internal
203.0.113.45 kms.internal # added by legacy-migration script
```

nate: that explains the mismatch: pods using cluster DNS saw 10.0.5.8 but processes that consult node hosts or node-local resolver (or init container running on node) might hit the external IP. need to check how the init container/probe resolves name (nsswitch.conf). can be a node-local caching resolver effect.

anita: containment plan: 1) rotate service-account tokens for key-manager-proxy 2) remove hosts override from bootstrap images and remediate node-12 3) revoke any external KMS grants to 203.0.113.45 until we verify scope 4) collect kube-apiserver audit lines, node syslogs, and pod filesystem snapshot for forensics. commands: `kubectl delete secret -n priv-core sa-key-manager-token-XXXX` and `kubectl rollout restart deploy/key-manager -n priv-core`.

forensics-bot: artifacts collected: kube-audit slice (11:00-11:20), node-12 /etc/hosts snapshot, pod /var/run/secrets tarball. Uploaded to INC-2026-900.

sara: additional notes: why did preflight not catch this? our probe validated HTTP 200 but didn't validate the resolved IP against the cluster allowlist nor verify certificate SAN. add those checks: probe should assert IP in allowlist and TLS SAN includes kms.internal CN.

nate: I'll add a CI gate to run the enhanced probe in our canary cluster prior to RBAC changes and also ensure node bootstrap forbids hosts overrides: disallow legacy-migration script or make it idempotent.

anita: triage: no impersonation seen yet in the audit slice, but there are repeated GET /v1/decrypt calls from the SA token during 11:02-11:05; looks like the app replayed queued decrypts after the RBAC change. we need to confirm whether actual decrypts completed on the external KMS. if so, escalate to legal.

mike: containment actions executed: removed hosts entry on node-12, rotated SA token, forced rollout restart of key-manager, applied egress deny for 203.0.113.45 at VPC. monitoring for repeats.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-900 created (Priv-core KMS host mismatch). Assignees: anita, sara. Priority: P2.

sara: postmortem action items: 1) make preflight probe assert resolved IP allowlist + TLS SAN 2) block hosts overrides in node bootstrap 3) require short-lived SA tokens for secrets-access SAs 4) add alert for KMS-host hits from private clusters 5) run image scans for baked-in creds.

anita: I'll own the postmortem and coordinate vuln-triage. legal on standby if external decrypts confirmed. uploading timeline to the incident ticket.

mike: thanks all. adding links to artifacts and a short timeline into INC-2026-900 in case we need to notify customers.
